verification.note: Complete displayed signed original remembrance read through the web tool on the author’s original scholarly posting. Wright identifies his interviews for Cook’s biography and reports the specific Creighton and Kealey acknowledgments. Their underlying originals are not newly read. Local raw reading record is a reading/locator receipt rather than a downloaded article payload; ordinary local request was unavailable. Comments by Iacovetta and Greer were encountered as separate voices and do not establish a detailed intellectual debt.

sources.title: Donald Wright, “Ceci n’est pas Ramsay Cook: A Biographical Reconnaissance,” 2017
sources.citation: Donald Wright, “Ceci n’est pas Ramsay Cook: A Biographical Reconnaissance,” in Doug Munro and John G. Reid, eds., Clio’s Lives: Biographies and Autobiographies of Historians (ANU Press, 2017), 103–134.

verification.note: Original open publisher chapter PDF and HTML consulted. Read opening 103–105 and sections IV–V, 123–134, with corresponding notes 79–111, for early formation and the Lower/Gibson seminar, Acton reading and biography’s limits. Earlier childhood sections were encountered in searches but not read completely; no full-chapter claim. Stronger early teachers and the Acton resource lack full person nodes. Underlying interviews, memoirs, papers and thesis not read. This source supports held cases and bounded corroboration, not new full biographies.

pe135_cook_burden_1977.note: Complete own review 110–115 and its two notes freshly read in the original Acadiensis journal PDF. National versus regional focus, attribution to W. L. Morton, defined-region difficulties, shared benefits and shortcomings retained. Reviewed books, correspondence and underlying documents remain unread.

pe135_cook_unmasked_1983.note: Complete own review 137–142 and all eight notes freshly read in the original Acadiensis journal PDF. Berger’s historiographical framing at137 and the specific Cole Harris use138/141 support bounded personal-resource proposals. Graeme Wynn’s chapter receives the strongest chapter praise; his missing full endpoint is held. Cook’s qualified defense of class, sex, family and ethnicity research survives his rejection of regionalism as a general unit. Original chapters and cited books remain unread; the next review beginning on142 is a different signed text.

pe135_cook_atlantic_1993.note: Complete own review 146–152 freshly read in the original Acadiensis journal PDF. McKay149–150 is praised alongside Howell; Fingard and Reid receive similarly strong attention, and the closing argument keeps distinctiveness alongside shared historical processes. Book editors and chapter authors retain individual credit; no fresh whole-volume or chapter-original reading. Criticisms of contributors are Cook’s judgments, not independently certified factual errors.
